page.content:
Monsoon sea lanes from South China through the Indian Ocean.

How Maritime silk route connects

  • Topic: Silk Road — The monsoon sea lanes are the maritime half of the Silk Road.
  • Location: Quanzhou — Quanzhou was a chief Chinese port of the maritime silk route.
  • Faction: Srivijaya — Srivijaya taxed and policed a central stretch of the maritime route.
  • Item: Silk — Silk also moved on ships when monsoon freight undercut the caravan.

What is Maritime silk route?

The maritime silk route linked Guangzhou and Quanzhou to Srivijaya, India, the Persian Gulf, and the Red Sea. It carried more bulk than camels and, in some centuries, more religious traffic too.

Key threads lead to Silk Road, Quanzhou, Srivijaya and Silk.
